question: Buses come every 10 minutes on average, at random. Arriving at a random moment, how long do you wait on average?
answer: About 10 minutes, if arrivals are truly random. You are more likely to turn up during a long gap than a short one, so the gap you land in averages 20 minutes, and you wait half of it. Only buses keeping perfect time would make it 5.
move: Arriving at random lands you in the long gaps more often than the short.
ask: Where do I keep landing in the long gaps and blaming bad luck?
trap: Half the average gap, as if buses kept perfect time.
source: Feller, An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications, Volume II, 1971
reference: William Feller, An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications, Volume II, second edition, Wiley, 1971
